title: For RISC-V boards enablement (and also some ARM platforms if I'm not mistaken), it is always useful to be able to generate images with a custom kernel flavour.
description:
For RISC-V boards enablement (and also some ARM platforms if I'm not mistaken), it is always useful to be able to generate images with a custom kernel flavour.

Our experiments with Spacemit K3 have led to different flavours used: one k3-6.18 vendor kernel, and one k3-7.2 kernel with some patches cherry-picked.

We have added a 'k3' subarch to livecd-rootfs that only does KERNEL_FLAVOURS selection. Now we would need to add another 'k3-7.2' subarch to select our new 'k3-7.2' kernel flavour.

With that patch, the idea is that we could just pass 'kernel_flavours=k3-x.x' and not have a subarch at all anymore. This would help for future board enablement as well, as we usually only need a different kernel. A real subarch can be kept for official images or when something more than the kernel flavour needs to change.

@@ -305,3 +309,24 @@ Ubuntu-Server 26.04 LTS "Resolute Raccoon" - Release amd64 (20270210)
 We could do a `livecd-rootfs` upload to change this (it only changes once
 per cycle), but it's quicker and easier to manage this from the code that
 triggers the livefs builds.
+
+## `KERNEL_FLAVOURS`
+
+**Set with `build-livefs`:** `--kernel-flavours`
+
+The kernel flavour (or flavours) to build the image with, e.g. `generic` or
+`generic-hwe-26.04`. When this is not supplied, `live-build/auto/config`
+selects a sensible default per project, architecture and subarchitecture
+(e.g. `generic-hwe-26.04` for the desktop, `virtual` for cloud images,
+`none` for projects that handle their own kernel such as `ubuntu-server:live`).
+
+When it is supplied, the value overrides that per-project default at every
+point the kernel flavour is used: the `--linux-flavours` passed to `lb config`,
+the explicit `linux-<flavour>` package added to layers, and `DEFAULT_KERNEL`.
+The per-project arch/subarch corrections are skipped in this case (you get
+exactly what you asked for), so take care to request a flavour that actually
+exists for the target -- e.g. there is no `-hwe` kernel on `riscv64`.
+
+This is currently only reachable via the local `build-livefs` path (and
+`build-livefs-lxd`, which forwards it through); it is not yet wired through
+`launchpad-buildd` build metadata.

 # When building install-sources, what kernel is the default?

+# KERNEL_FLAVOURS may be supplied via the environment (e.g. by
+# build-livefs --kernel-flavours) to override the per-project default chosen
